label: Resting potential of distant cells controls oncogene-dependent tumorigenesis
claim: The resting membrane potentials of cells located at a distance from oncogene-expressing cells are critical for whether those oncogene-expressing cells go on to form tumors in vivo, as shown in Xenopus laevis tadpoles injected with human oncogenes.
quote: Extending prior work focused on the bioelectric state of cancer cells themselves, we show for the first time that the resting potentials of distant cells are critical for oncogene-dependent tumorigenesis.
scope: Xenopus laevis embryos/tadpoles injected with human or Xenopus oncogene mRNAs (Xrel3, Gli1, KRASG12D)
measurable_quantities: resting membrane potential (Vmem) of cells remote from the oncogene-injected site
incidence of induced tumor-like structures per embryo
distance between hyperpolarized and oncogene-expressing regions
candidate_data: Xenopus voltage-reporter dye imaging and tumor-incidence scoring datasets, Xenbase gene expression and phenotype records for ion channels and oncogenes, and image repositories such as the Image Data Resource or the Cell Image Library.

label: Oncogene-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus share hallmarks of human tumors
claim: Tumor-like structures induced in Xenopus laevis tadpoles by human oncogenes such as mutant KRAS display overproliferation, increased nuclear size, hypoxia, intracellular acidity and leukocyte attraction, hallmarks shared with classic human tumors.
quote: In the Xenopus laevis tadpole model, we used human oncogenes such as mutant KRAS to drive formation of tumor-like structures that exhibited overproliferation, increased nuclear size, hypoxia, acidity, and leukocyte attraction.
scope: Induced tumor-like structures (ITLS) in Xenopus laevis embryos injected with Xrel3, Gli1 or KRASG12D mRNA
measurable_quantities: fraction of cells in G2/S/M phase (FUCCI reporter)
leukocyte density at the tumor site
candidate_data: Xenopus histology and fluorescence imaging deposited in the Image Data Resource or Cell Image Library, Xenbase phenotype annotations, and comparable human tumor histopathology and hypoxia-marker datasets.

label: Remote Kv1.5 hyperpolarization suppresses tumor-like structures from two oncogenes
claim: In Xenopus laevis embryos, misexpressing the hyperpolarizing potassium channel Kv1.5 in a blastomere distant from the oncogene-injected blastomere reduces the incidence of induced tumor-like structures by about 35% for Xrel3 and about 29% for Gli1, indicating the suppression is not specific to one oncogene.
quote: Kv1.5-induced long-distance hyperpolarization was also able to significantly suppress Xrel3 and Gli1 ITLS formation by 34.9% (N=225; t-test, P<0.05) and 29.4% (N=292; t-test, P<0.05), respectively (Fig. 2C), suggesting the effect is not specific for just one type of oncogene.
scope: 16-cell-stage Xenopus laevis embryos co-injected with Xrel3 or Gli1 and Kv1.5 mRNA in separate blastomeres, scored at stage 34
candidate_data: The paper's own tumor-incidence counts, Xenbase ion-channel misexpression phenotype records, and electrophysiology or voltage-dye imaging datasets for Kv1.5 overexpression.

label: High-chloride hyperpolarization suppresses KRAS tumors, so the effect is ion-independent
claim: Raising extracellular chloride, which hyperpolarizes cells through native chloride channels, decreases the incidence of KRASG12D-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus laevis embryos by about 38%, showing that tumor suppression depends on the change in membrane voltage rather than on the Kv1.5 channel or on potassium specifically.
quote: Treatment with high chloride (whose uptake by native Cl− channels hyperpolarizes cells) resulted in a 37.5% decrease (N=349; t-test P<0.05) in KRASG12D ITLS, demonstrating that the suppressive effect is not specific for Kv1.5 nor for potassium, as mediators of the crucial Vmem change (Fig. 2C).
scope: Xenopus laevis embryos injected with KRASG12D mRNA and raised in elevated (70 mM) chloride medium
measurable_quantities: resting membrane potential of host cells
candidate_data: The paper's own incidence counts under high and low chloride, Xenopus electrophysiology datasets on chloride-driven hyperpolarization, and Xenbase developmental phenotype records.

label: Native CLIC1 mediates chloride-based long-range tumor suppression
claim: The endogenous chloride intracellular channel 1 (CLIC1) is required for chloride-driven, long-range suppression of oncogene-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus laevis, because non-local overexpression of wildtype CLIC1 increases suppression while a dominant-negative CLIC1C24S mutant blocks suppression even under high extracellular chloride.
quote: In contrast, overexpression of the mutant CLIC1 (N=336) effectively blocked ITLS suppression despite the presence of high Cl− (Fig 4C). Together, these data suggest a role for native CLIC1 in mediating hyperpolarization-induced long-range ITLS suppression.
scope: 16-cell-stage Xenopus laevis embryos injected with KRASG12D plus wildtype or dominant-negative CLIC1 in a separate blastomere, raised in 70 mM chloride
measurable_quantities: CLIC1 expression level and spatial distribution
candidate_data: Xenbase CLIC1 expression and morpholino/misexpression records, Oncomine-style tumor expression profiles for CLIC1, and gene-expression data in the Gene Expression Omnibus for CLIC1 in tumors.

label: HDAC1 activity transduces remote voltage change into tumor suppression
claim: Histone deacetylase 1 activity is the main transduction step by which hyperpolarization of distant cells suppresses tumorigenesis in Xenopus laevis, since expressing a dominant-negative HDAC1 at a site remote from KRASG12D-expressing cells raises the incidence of induced tumor-like structures by about 36%.
quote: introducing DN-HDAC1 non-locally to the site of KRASG12D increased ITLS formation incidence by 35.6% (χ2, P<0.05) (Fig. 5C), suggesting a role for histone deacetylase 1 activity controlling cell behavior at a distance.
scope: Xenopus laevis embryos injected with KRASG12D and dominant-negative HDAC1 mRNA in separate blastomeres under hyperpolarizing high-chloride conditions
candidate_data: Histone acetylation and HDAC1 ChIP-seq or expression datasets in the Gene Expression Omnibus, Xenbase HDAC1 expression records, and the paper's own incidence counts.

label: Antibiotics against gram-positive bacteria increase tumor incidence
claim: Treating Xenopus laevis embryos with antibiotics that target gram-positive bacteria — novobiocin alone, or a cocktail of gentamicin, metronidazole, vancomycin and clindamycin — significantly increases the incidence of oncogene-induced tumor-like structures, implying that native butyrate-producing bacteria normally restrain tumorigenesis.
quote: Finally, a cocktail of antibiotics (gentamicin, metrodinazole, vancomycin hydrochloride, and clindamycin hydrochloride, all at 20 μM concentration) targeting gram-positive bacteria resulted in a significant increase in ITLS incidence by 26.2% (χ2, P<0.05) (Fig. 6).
scope: Oncogene-injected Xenopus laevis embryos exposed to antibiotics in the rearing medium
candidate_data: 16S rRNA amplicon and metagenomic surveys of the Xenopus and vertebrate microbiome in the Sequence Read Archive or MG-RAST, short-chain fatty acid metabolomics datasets, and epidemiological antibiotic-exposure and cancer-risk studies.

label: Vmem controls tumorigenesis via bacterially derived butyrate acting on HDAC1
claim: Control of oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis by resting membrane potential in Xenopus laevis is mediated by histone deacetylase 1, whose inhibition depends on butyrate produced by native gram-positive bacteria.
quote: Together, these data suggest that the control of tumorigenesis by Vmem is mediated by HDAC1, via butyrate derived from gram-positive bacteria.
scope: Oncogene-injected Xenopus laevis embryos with hyperpolarizing treatments, antibiotic treatments and dominant-negative HDAC1
candidate_data: Short-chain fatty acid metabolomic data, microbiome sequencing in the Sequence Read Archive, histone-acetylation profiling in the Gene Expression Omnibus, and SLC5A8 butyrate-transport electrophysiology literature data.

label: Hyperpolarization skews butyrate-producing bacteria toward depolarized oncogene cells
claim: In the model the authors propose, hyperpolarized cells present a positively charged outer surface that reduces bacterial viability, so butyrate-producing bacteria are distributed away from hyperpolarized cells and toward the depolarized oncogene-expressing cells, where the resulting butyrate inhibits HDAC and promotes histone hyperacetylation and cell cycle arrest.
quote: As a result, distribution of butyrate producing-bacteria is skewed away from hyperpolarized cells in favor of oncogene-expressing cells, which are known to be depolarized pre-neoplastic transformation [43].
scope: Proposed model for Xenopus laevis embryos bearing oncogene-induced tumor-like structures and hyperpolarized remote tissue
measurable_quantities: cell-surface charge as a function of Vmem
spatial distribution and viability of butyrate-producing bacteria
candidate_data: Bacterial adhesion and surface-charge measurements in the literature, spatially resolved microbiome imaging data, and short-chain fatty acid metabolomics; no deposited dataset is named in the paper.

label: Resting potential as a systems-level causal factor rather than specific channels
claim: Because tumor suppression was obtained with either chloride- or potassium-based hyperpolarization, the authors argue that a systems-level physiological property — resting membrane potential — rather than any specific ion channel acting as an oncogene or tumor suppressor, can be a powerful causal factor regulating tumorigenesis.
quote: Thus, in complement to the gene-focused idea of specific ion channels being intrinsic oncogenes or tumor suppressors [44, 48, 145], we suggest that a systems-level physiological property – resting potential – can be a powerful causal factor in regulating these processes.
scope: Bioelectric control of tumorigenesis generally, argued from Xenopus laevis oncogene experiments
measurable_quantities: resting membrane potential achieved by different channels and ions
incidence of tumor-like structures across channel and ion manipulations
candidate_data: Comparative datasets of tumor incidence under distinct channel/ion manipulations that produce matched Vmem shifts; Xenbase and Gene Expression Omnibus ion-channel expression resources.

label: Tumors may themselves emit bioelectric information detectable at a distance
claim: The authors speculate that long-range bioelectric connections in tumorigenesis are bidirectional, so that in addition to remote tissue voltage influencing tumor growth, tumors may emit bioelectric information that could be detected at a distance.
quote: It is tempting to speculate that the long-range connections are bi-directional: not only does remote electrical state of tissue matter for tumor growth, but perhaps tumors also emit bioelectrical information that could be detectable at a distance.
scope: Tumor–host bioelectric signaling, to be tested with molecular reagents in Xenopus and other models
measurable_quantities: voltage reporter signal in tissue remote from a tumor
spatial decay of any tumor-associated Vmem change
distance between tumor and detector site
candidate_data: Voltage-reporter and electrophysiological imaging datasets of tumor-bearing animals, including classical bioelectric tumor-detection measurements; no specific deposited dataset is named.

label: If conserved in mammals, Vmem modulation offers cancer detection and treatment routes
claim: The authors predict that if the role of remote endogenous bioelectric states in tumorigenesis is conserved in mammalian cancer models, modulation of resting membrane potential — potentially with ion channel drugs already approved for human use — would provide new cancer detection and treatment modalities.
quote: Future work must also examine the roles of remote endogenous bioelectric states in mammalian cancer models; if conserved, these data suggest a number of detection and treatment modalities focused on Vmem modulation.
scope: Mammalian cancer models and, by extension, human cancer therapy
measurable_quantities: resting membrane potential in mammalian host tissue
tumor incidence and growth under ion channel drug treatment
candidate_data: Rodent tumor model studies of ion channel drugs, pharmacology resources such as ChEMBL and DrugBank, and tumor expression datasets in the Gene Expression Omnibus or The Cancer Genome Atlas.
